paragraphs.text: Grist , known as the Hunger Tide , is an insect planeswalker from an undisclosed plane .

Grist creates an essence that inhabits insect swarms on the planes it travels to. When Grist planeswalks, there is a bright flash of light in the sky, a harbinger for farmers of the coming plague of insects. The same flash happens when it planeswalks away. Grist has access to black and green mana .

Each enemy devoured by Grist creates a stronger swarm, as it not only feeds on bodies but also on magical potency as well. Perhaps the spark it uses to travel from world to world belonged to one of its countless victims...

In Grist's non- canon Boom! Comics appearances, it is described as female and uses she/her pronouns. In its Modern Horizons 3 printing, Grist was referred to using it/its pronouns. When the discrepancy was noted, Mark Rosewater stated that although Grist is female, it may use non-gendered pronouns.
Grist's nature as a collective-entity planeswalker was concepted by Creative long before its black-bordered card printing in Modern Horizons 2 .

For years, Grist had traveled the planes, arriving at locations where vegetation was ready for consumption. After about a week, she would summon a swarm of biblical proportions from the local host of insects and would lead the swarm to a feast that would leave the land dry as a bone. At times, she would call the swarm into a condensed form, acting as one, creating the illusion of a horrible zombie-like creature. Kamigawa and Eldraine were two such locations ravaged by Grist.

Tamiyo , noticing similar stories across the Multiverse of large numbers of insects that devastated farming communities, sought out Ajani Goldmane to help her solve the mystery of the flashes that appeared before and after each of these events. Ajani searched the swarm for a soul with a spark and, in doing so, discovered and spoke with Grist. Just as Ajani was unaware that such planeswalkers existed as Grist, Grist had been unaware that humans/humanoids were people or that she had been hurting them. Tamiyo suggested that Grist and her swarm feed on the Wilds of Eldraine instead of the fields planted by the hurting village of Mossverge, and Grist agreed to relocate the feast and not eat the bark from the trees, so that the leaves would regrow in time. Ajani and Tamiyo agreed that Grist had committed no crime yet, but that if she resumed knowingly destroying fields constructed by people, they would then know whether she could be trusted. For now, Grist is a friend.
